blocks.text: Genesis presents Adam and Eve as the first human pair. Humanity is created in God’s image, and the account describes life in Eden, the command concerning the tree and the relationship of man and woman. These passages establish the biblical setting of their names and their place in Christian teaching about humanity.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The serpent’s temptation, the eating of the forbidden fruit and the attempt to hide from God are narrated in Genesis 3. The consequences include suffering, exclusion from Eden and mortality. The story also records God’s provision of clothing. This profile follows the text without supplying imagined conversations beyond it.

sections.title: Death and limits of the account

blocks.text: Genesis reports Adam’s death at 930 years of age. It does not give an equivalent account of Eve’s death. These are the scriptural narratives; neither a modern absolute chronology nor a separate martyrdom story is established here.

blocks.text: The OCA explicitly includes Adam and Eve in the Sunday before the Nativity. Their commemoration belongs to that movable Sunday, rather than a fixed date taken from one year’s calendar.
